messages:
oliver: quick check-in on auth surface: proposal to ban org-wide wildcard API keys from runtime service use by default. require project-scoped keys or brokered short-lived tokens.
priya: +1 on principle. what's the immediate migration pain? we have some infra jobs using org keys.
eva: propose detection-only mode for 10 days to build an owner list, then gradual deny-by-default with an allowlist for operator principals.
kevin: where to enforce? gateway seems best so we can toggle per-cluster and emit metrics. infra-bot: policy staged: enforce_scope=v1 mode=detect gateway=canary.
priya: UX: when creating org keys show a warning and default TTL=7d. add a checkbox "allow runtime use" that creates an allowlist request.
eva: long-term: build an "assume-project" broker. services authenticate with their principal and broker mints time-bound project tokens based on ACLs. avoids long-lived per-project keys.
oliver: tracing/audit: propagate origin_key_id and broker_claim to logs and traces. make sure SIEM can link actions to original principal.
kevin: edge case: bulk batch jobs that iterate many projects. broker should support batched minting or scoped wildcard with short TTL. document in RFC.
priya: agree. I'll draft the RFC and include migration checklist: detect-only, owner notifications, deploy-lint rule, allowlist workflow, broker PoC.
eva: can review Friday.
kevin: can review.
infra-bot: ticket created INFRA-5055 to track broker PoC and INFRA-5056 for gateway rollout.
